body.heading: The list as a lens
paragraphs: Writers have long used lists to capture a scene: things seen on a walk, sounds in a kitchen, objects on a desk. A list slows your attention down to one item at a time.
Try 'Things my grandmother kept in her apron pocket' or 'Sounds of the house at 6 a.m.' The title does half the work; the items do the rest.

body.heading: Choose, order, stop
paragraphs: Write more items than you need, then cross out the dull ones. Keep the specific and the surprising: not 'birds' but 'one crow, arguing with a bin'.
Order matters. End on the item that lingers. Then stop. A list poem is allowed to be seven lines long and finished, and brevity is part of its charm.

takeaway: Pick a title, gather specific things, and end on the one that lingers.
